Reward (3.1.2 and 3.2.2)¶

+1 for a new hit and -1 for a miss. A win already gets 10 from step(). Every game has exactly 9 hits, so over a game that takes T turns the return is about 18 - T, which means the only way to get more reward is to finish faster. Just counting hits would be the "be careful" case, since shooting a hit cell again would keep paying out. Here that gets -1 like a miss. I use the same reward for all three agents.

In [4]:
#@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
#two classes for these two environments
#@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
class Battleship:
    '''A class to manage the board'''
    
    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def __init__(self, config):
        '''Set up the constructor
            Takes -- config, a dictionary specifying the track dimensions and initial state
        '''
        self.config = config
        self.hit_streak = 0
        self.true_state = np.zeros([config['n'],config['n']],dtype = int)
        self.state = np.zeros([config['n'],config['n']],dtype = int)    #TODO -- consider how to change this
        self.old_state = copy.deepcopy(self.state)

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def position_maker(self,ship):
        '''A function to choose a position for a ship
            Takes:
                self -- class instance info above
                ship -- int, the index in the list of ship lengths
            Returns:
                an int, int pair, the coordinates of the first cell the ship occupies
        '''
        coord_1 = np.random.choice(list(range(self.config['n'] - self.config['ships'][ship] + 1)))    #choose first coordinate, guaranteed to have ship on board
        coord_2 = np.random.choice(list(range(self.config['n'])))    #choose second coordinate
        return coord_1,coord_2

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def check_empty(self,coord_1,coord_2,vert,ship):
        '''A function to make sure the proposed location is currently empty
            Takes:
                self -- class instance info above
                coord_1 -- int, the first coordinate, constrained to ensure the ship lies on the board
                coord_2 -- int, the second coordinate
                vert -- boolean, whether to orient the ship vertically or horizontally
                ship -- int, the index in the list of ship lengths
            Returns:
                a boolean, indicating if the placement is legal
        '''
        if vert:    #if the ship is oriented vertically...
            if sum(self.true_state[coord_1 + list(range(self.config['ships'][ship])),coord_2]) > 0:    #and if there is another ship lying across its path...
                empty = False    #set the empty indicator to false
            else:    #otherwise if the proposed location is empty...
                empty = True    #set the empty indicator to true
        else:    #if the ship is oriented horizontally...
            if sum(self.true_state[coord_2,coord_1 + list(range(self.config['ships'][ship]))]) > 0:    #and if there is anther ship lying across its path...
                empty = False    #set the empty indicator to false
            else:    #otherwise if the proposed location is empty...
                empty = True    #set the empty indicator to true
        return empty

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def place_ship(self,ship):
        '''A function to put a single ship on the board
            Takes:
                self -- class instance info above
                ship -- int, the index in the list of ship lengths
        '''
        empty = False    #init the stopping criterion
        while not empty:    #while we should keep going...
            coord_1,coord_2 = self.position_maker(ship)    #sample a position for the ship
            vert = np.random.uniform() < 0.5    #choose whether ship is horizontal or vertical
            empty = self.check_empty(coord_1,coord_2,vert,ship)    #check if legal
        if vert:    #if the ship is vertical...
            self.true_state[coord_1 + list(range(self.config['ships'][ship])),coord_2] = 1    #place on board
        else:    #if the ship is horizontal...
            self.true_state[coord_2,coord_1 + list(range(self.config['ships'][ship]))] = 1    #place on board
        vert = np.random.uniform() < 0.5    #choose whether ship is horizontal or vertical

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def make_board(self):
        '''A function to put all ships on the board
            Takes:
                self -- class instance info above
        '''
        self.true_state = np.zeros([self.config['n'],self.config['n']],dtype = int)
        for j in range(len(self.config['ships'])):    #loop over ship lengths
            self.place_ship(j)    #put on board'

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def reset(self):
        '''A function to reset the board
            Takes:
                self -- class instance info above
        '''
        self.hit_streak = 0
        self.true_state = np.zeros([self.config['n'],self.config['n']],dtype = int)    #reset the hidden state
        self.make_board()    #place ships again
        self.state = np.zeros([self.config['n'],self.config['n']],dtype = int)    #reset the observed state
        self.old_state = copy.deepcopy(self.state)
        

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def check_win(self):
        '''A function to check whether the agent has won
            Takes:
                self -- class instance info above
            Returns:
                a boolean, indicating if the agent sank all the ships
        '''
        if np.sum(self.state>0) == sum(self.config['ships']):    #if the number of hits is equal to the total length of ships...
            return True    #return true -- the agent won!
        else:    #otherwise...
            return False    #return false -- the game is still going

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def reward(self,):
        '''+1 for a new hit, -1 for a miss (or a wasted shot on a cell that's already a hit)'''
        if np.sum(self.state == 1) > np.sum(self.old_state == 1):
            return 1
        return -1

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def step(self,a):
        '''A function to update the state given the true enemy fleet locations'''
        if self.true_state[a['row'],a['col']] > 0:    #if there is a ship at the chosen location...
            self.state[a['row'],a['col']] = 1    #record a hit on the observed state as a 1
        else:    #if there is no ship
            self.state[a['row'],a['col']] = -1    #record a miss on the observed state as a -1
        done = self.check_win()    #check to see if the agent has won
        if done:
            r = 10#max(10*np.sum(self.state == 0),10)
        else:
            r = self.reward()    #WILL NOT WORK RIGHT NOW -- NEED TO SPECIFIY REWARD FUNCTION
        self.old_state = copy.deepcopy(self.state)
        return{'state':self.state,'reward':r,'done':done}

#@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
#A simple CNN architecture
class CNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(CNN, self).__init__()

        # Input: (batch_size, 1, 6, 6)
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(in_channels=1, out_channels=32, kernel_size=3, padding=1)  # -> (32, 6, 6)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(32, 64, kernel_size=3, padding=1)  # -> (64, 6, 6)
        self.conv3 = nn.Conv2d(64, 1, kernel_size=1)  # -> (1, 6, 6)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = F.relu(self.conv1(x))  # (batch_size, 32, 6, 6)
        x = F.relu(self.conv2(x))  # (batch_size, 64, 6, 6)
        q_map = self.conv3(x)      # (batch_size, 1, 6, 6)
        return q_map.squeeze(1)    # -> (batch_size, 6, 6)

DQN agent (3.2)¶

This fills in the TODOs in the starter Agent. The state is just the board (1 = hit, -1 = miss, 0 = not shot) fed to the CNN, which outputs one Q-value per cell. All my agents can only shoot cells that haven't been shot yet, so pi and the target both take the max over untargeted cells only.

In [6]:
#@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
class Agent:
    '''A class to manage the chase'''
    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def __init__(self, config):
        '''Set up the constructor
            Takes -- config, a dictionary specifying the track dimensions and initial state
        '''
        self.config = config    #save the config file
        self.A_s = self.config['A']    #save the action set
        self.Q = CNN()    #init the deep learning model
        self.Q_target = copy.deepcopy(self.Q)    #copy the target approximator
        self.buffer = []    #init the replay buffer
        self.optimizer = optim.Adam(self.Q.parameters(), lr=self.config['alpha'])

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def update_Q_target(self,):
        '''A function to update the target approximator
        '''
        self.Q_target.load_state_dict(self.Q.state_dict())

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def purge_replay_buffer(self,):
        '''A function to keep the replay buffer within memory limits
        '''
        if len(self.buffer) > self.config['M']:
            self.buffer.pop(0)    #drop the oldest tuple

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def forward_pass(self, net, s):
        '''A function to compute the forward pass
            s is a stack of boards (batch, 6, 6), returns Q-values (batch, 36)
        '''
        x = torch.as_tensor(s, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(1)    #add the channel dim the CNN wants
        return net(x).reshape(len(x), -1)

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def pi(self, s, epsilon):
        '''A function to choose actions using Q-values
        '''
        cells = legal(s)
        if np.random.rand() < epsilon:
            return np.random.choice(cells)
        with torch.no_grad():
            q = self.forward_pass(self.Q, s[None])[0].numpy()
        return cells[np.argmax(q[cells])]

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def make_batch(self):
        '''A function to make a batch for updating Q
        '''
        idx = np.random.randint(len(self.buffer), size=self.config['B'])
        s, a, r, s2, done = zip(*[self.buffer[i] for i in idx])
        return (np.array(s), torch.tensor(np.array(a)), torch.tensor(r, dtype=torch.float32),
                np.array(s2), torch.tensor(done, dtype=torch.float32))

    #@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@@
    def update_Q_value(self, batch):
        '''A function to use the batch to estimate the gradient and take a single step
        '''
        s, a, r, s2, done = batch
        q = self.forward_pass(self.Q, s).gather(1, a[:, None]).squeeze(1)    #Q(s,a) for the actions taken
        with torch.no_grad():
            q2 = self.forward_pass(self.Q_target, s2)
            q2[torch.as_tensor(s2.reshape(len(s2), -1) != 0)] = -1e9    #can't shoot a cell twice (not -inf, 0*-inf is nan)
            y = r + self.config['gamma'] * (1 - done) * q2.max(1).values
        loss = F.mse_loss(q, y)
        self.optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        self.optimizer.step()

Config¶

The starter config cell, unchanged. DQN uses it as-is. The tabular agents use the same gamma and epsilon but a bigger step size (alpha = 0.1), since 0.001 would barely move a Q table.

In [8]:
N_EPS = 20000    #training episodes per agent
CHECKPOINTS = [500, 5000, 10000, 20000]    #save + evaluate the agent here
tab_config = dict(agent_config, alpha=0.1)

def legal(s):
    '''cells that haven't been shot yet, as indices into A'''
    return np.flatnonzero(s.flatten() == 0)

def play(pi_fn, n_games):
    '''play n_games where pi_fn maps a board to a cell index, returns the turns each game took'''
    env = Battleship(env_config)
    turns = []
    for g in range(n_games):
        env.reset()
        done, t = False, 0
        while not done:
            a = pi_fn(env.state.copy())
            done = env.step({'row': A[a][0], 'col': A[a][1]})['done']
            t += 1
        turns.append(t)
    return turns

Classical Q-learning (3.1)¶

One tabular Q-learning class handles both agents. The only difference is key(s), which gives the Q-table key for shooting each cell on board s. Update is the usual Q-learning one, Q(k) += alpha * (r + gamma * max over untargeted cells of Q(s') - Q(k)).

Agent 1 (raw board): the key is (board, cell). There are up to 3^36 boards, so almost every state it sees is new and it should basically play randomly.

Agent 2 (my features): instead of describing the whole board, I describe the cell being shot, so the action is "shoot a cell that looks like this" and the agent picks whichever untargeted cell has the best type. Three features per cell:

  • hits: how many of its 4 neighbors are hits (0, 1, 2+). Ships are next to hits.
  • line: 1 if the cell continues two hits in a row in some direction, which points along a ship.
  • fit: how many ways a ship (length 2, 3 or 4, either direction) could be placed over this cell without covering a miss, bucketed as min(count // 4, 4). Middle cells and open areas score high, cells boxed in by misses or the edge score low.

That's 3 * 2 * 5 = 30 states total.

In [10]:
FEATURES = ('hits', 'line', 'fit')

def features(s):
    '''feature grids (6x6) for every cell of board s'''
    n = env_config['n']
    h = np.pad(s == 1, 2)    #hits, padded so neighbors of edge cells are "not a hit"
    c = slice(2, -2)
    up, down, left, right = h[1:-3, c], h[3:-1, c], h[c, 1:-3], h[c, 3:-1]
    hits = up.astype(int) + down + left + right
    line = (up & h[:-4, c]) | (down & h[4:, c]) | (left & h[c, :-4]) | (right & h[c, 4:])

    ok = s != -1    #cells a ship could still be on
    fit = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=int)
    for L in env_config['ships']:
        for d in range(n - L + 1):
            fit[:, d:d+L] += ok[:, d:d+L].all(1)[:, None]    #horizontal placements starting at col d
            fit[d:d+L, :] += ok[d:d+L, :].all(0)[None, :]    #vertical placements starting at row d
    return {'hits': np.minimum(hits, 2), 'line': line.astype(int), 'fit': np.minimum(fit // 4, 4)}

def raw_key(s):
    b = (s + 1).astype(np.int8).tobytes()    #board as 36 bytes
    return [(b, a) for a in range(len(A))]

def feature_key(s, feats=FEATURES):
    f = features(s)
    return list(zip(*[f[name].flatten().tolist() for name in feats]))

class QAgent:
    '''tabular Q-learning, key(s) gives the Q-table key for shooting each cell of board s'''
    def __init__(self, config, key):
        self.config = config
        self.key = key
        self.Q = {}    #unseen keys are 0

    def q_values(self, s):
        return np.array([self.Q.get(k, 0.0) for k in self.key(s)])

    def pi(self, s, epsilon):
        '''epsilon-greedy over untargeted cells, ties broken randomly'''
        cells = legal(s)
        if np.random.rand() < epsilon:
            return np.random.choice(cells)
        q = self.q_values(s)[cells]
        return np.random.choice(cells[q == q.max()])

    def update(self, s, a, r, s2, done):
        k = self.key(s)[a]
        target = r if done else r + self.config['gamma'] * self.q_values(s2)[legal(s2)].max()
        self.Q[k] = self.Q.get(k, 0.0) + self.config['alpha'] * (target - self.Q.get(k, 0.0))

Training (3.3)¶

This is the starter training loop filled in. DQN does what the starter comments say (buffer, purge, update Q every n_steps_for_Q_update steps, copy to the target every C steps). The tabular agents just do their update each turn. I record the reward and turns of every episode. At 500, 5000, 10000 and 20000 episodes I save the agent to models/ and play 500 greedy (epsilon = 0) games to see how good it is at that point.

In [11]:
def train(agent, name, n_eps=N_EPS):
    dqn = isinstance(agent, Agent)
    board = Battleship(env_config)
    rows, evals = [], []
    steps = 0
    for epi in tqdm(range(n_eps), desc=name, mininterval=10):    #loop over episodes
        board.make_board()    #set up the board
        done = False    #set the stopping condition
        turn = 0    #init the turn count
        G = 0
        while not done:    #while the episode goes on...
            s = board.state.copy()    #save the old state
            a = agent.pi(s, agent.config['epsilon'])    #generate an action
            out = board.step({'row': A[a][0], 'col': A[a][1]})    #evolve the environment
            r, s2, done = out['reward'], out['state'].copy(), out['done']    #reward, new state, whether we've stopped
            if dqn:
                agent.buffer.append((s, a, r, s2, done))    #add this tuple to the replay buffer
                agent.purge_replay_buffer()    #remove the oldest tuple if appropriate
                steps += 1
                if steps % agent.config['n_steps_for_Q_update'] == 0 and len(agent.buffer) >= agent.config['B']:
                    agent.update_Q_value(agent.make_batch())    #update the Q values
                if steps % agent.config['C'] == 0:
                    agent.update_Q_target()    #update the target approximator
            else:
                agent.update(s, a, r, s2, done)
            G += r
            turn += 1
        board.reset()    #reset the board
        rows.append({'agent': name, 'episode': epi + 1, 'reward': G, 'turns': turn})

        if epi + 1 in CHECKPOINTS:
            if dqn:
                torch.save(agent.Q.state_dict(), f"models/{name}_{epi + 1}.pt")
            else:
                with open(f"models/{name}_{epi + 1}.pkl", "wb") as f:
                    pickle.dump(agent.Q, f)
            evals.append({'agent': name, 'episode': epi + 1,
                          'greedy turns': np.mean(play(lambda s: agent.pi(s, 0), 500))})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows), pd.DataFrame(evals)

def plot_curves(dfs, title, filename):
    '''dfs maps a label to a training dataframe, curves are 100 episode moving averages'''
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4))
    for label, df in dfs.items():
        axes[0].plot(df['episode'], df['reward'].rolling(100, min_periods=1).mean(), label=label)
        axes[1].plot(df['episode'], df['turns'].rolling(100, min_periods=1).mean(), label=label)
    axes[1].axhline(np.mean(random_turns), color='gray', ls='--', label='random (mean)')
    for ax, y in zip(axes, ['reward per episode', 'turns to finish']):
        ax.set_title(title + ': ' + y)
        ax.set_xlabel('training episode')
        ax.set_ylabel(y + ' (100 episode avg)')
    axes[1].legend()
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("figures/" + filename, dpi=150)
    plt.show()

What the agents learned (Q5)¶
Q-value of every cell on two boards: an empty board, and a board from partway through a random game right after
a hit. H = hit, M = miss (those cells are blanked since they can't be shot), and the star is the cell the
greedy agent would pick.


















In [14]:






example = Battleship(env_config)
example.reset()
while True:    #shoot randomly until there's a fresh hit and at least 8 cells shot
    a = np.random.choice(legal(example.state))
    out = example.step({'row': A[a][0], 'col': A[a][1]})
    if out['reward'] == 1 and np.sum(example.state != 0) >= 8:
        break
boards = {'empty board': np.zeros((6, 6), dtype=int), 'mid-game board': example.state.copy()}

def q_map(ag, s):
    if isinstance(ag, Agent):
        with torch.no_grad():
            q = ag.forward_pass(ag.Q, s[None])[0].numpy()
    else:
        q = ag.q_values(s)
    q = q.astype(float).reshape(6, 6)
    q[s != 0] = np.nan    #already shot
    return q

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(15, 9))
for i, (bname, s) in enumerate(boards.items()):
    for j, (name, ag) in enumerate(agents.items()):
        ax = axes[i, j]
        im = ax.imshow(q_map(ag, s), cmap='viridis')
        for (r, c), v in np.ndenumerate(s):
            if v != 0:
                ax.text(c, r, 'H' if v == 1 else 'M', ha='center', va='center', color='red' if v == 1 else 'black')
        best = ag.pi(s, 0)
        ax.scatter(best % 6, best // 6, marker='*', color='white', edgecolor='black', s=250)
        fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
        ax.set_title(name + ', ' + bname)
        ax.set_xlabel('col')
        ax.set_ylabel('row')
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("figures/policy_heatmaps.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()

Ablations (4)¶
Features: retrain agent 2 three times, each time without one of the features. DQN: retrain with C = 1,
so the target network gets overwritten by the online network every step, which is the same as not having a
target network. Everything else stays the same. Sample efficiency shows up in the training curves and the
early checkpoints, and final performance is the 20000 episode checkpoint.


















In [16]:






abl_curves = {'all features': curves['agent2_features']}
abl_evals = [evals['agent2_features']]
for drop in FEATURES:
    keep = tuple(f for f in FEATURES if f != drop)
    name = 'agent2_no_' + drop
    df, ev = train(QAgent(tab_config, lambda s, keep=keep: feature_key(s, keep)), name)
    abl_curves['no ' + drop] = df
    abl_evals.append(ev)

dqn_df, dqn_ev = train(Agent(dict(agent_config, C=1)), 'dqn_no_target')
abl_evals += [evals['dqn'], dqn_ev]

pd.concat([df.assign(run=label) for label, df in abl_curves.items()] + [dqn_df]).to_csv(
    "results/ablation_curves.csv", index=False)
ablation_summary = pd.concat(abl_evals).pivot(index='agent', columns='episode', values='greedy turns')
